---
title: "Physiological Processes"
---

iLand models the continuous physiological processes that govern energy capture, resource competition, and biogeochemical cycling at individual tree and landscape levels.

### [Resource Availability and Competition](resource-availability-and-competition.qmd)

Spatially explicit competition among individual trees for above- and belowground resources:

* **[Light Competition](competition-for-light.qmd):** 3D canopy light absorption based on Light Influence Patterns ([LIPs](individual-tree-light-availability.qmd)).
* **[Belowground Competition](competition-for-belowground-resources.qmd):** Competition for soil water and nitrogen mediated by root distribution and soil properties.

### [Primary Production](primary-production.qmd)

Radiation absorption and gross primary production calculated using a hierarchical approach derived from the 3-PG model:

* **[Environmental Modifiers](constraints-to-resource-utilization.qmd):** Response functions modulating productivity based on [temperature](temperature-response.qmd), [vapor pressure deficit](vapor-pressure-deficit-response.qmd), [atmospheric CO₂](co2-response.qmd), [soil water](soil-water-response.qmd), and [soil nitrogen](nitrogen-response.qmd).
* **[Phenology](phenology.qmd):** Seasonal dynamics of foliage flush, senescence, and growing season length.

### [Carbon Allocation](allocation.qmd) & [Stem Growth](stem-growth.qmd)

Partitioning of net primary production (NPP) into foliage, fine roots, and woody biomass pools based on pipe-model allometry and resource limitations.

### [Water Cycle](water-cycle.qmd)

Canopy interception, evapotranspiration, snowpack accumulation/melt, and soil water percolation:

* **[Landscape Soil Water Dynamics](landscape-scale-soil-water-dynamics.qmd):** Lateral redistribution of soil water across topography on landscape scales.

### [Soil Dynamics](soil-dynamics.qmd) & [Biogeochemical Cycling](soil-c-and-n-cycling.qmd)

Litter decomposition, soil organic matter turnover, and nutrient mineralization based on the Century/ICBM soil models.
